claims.statement: A RunTree models a root trace or child run with per-run id and parent_run_id, while all descendants inherit the root trace_id and extend the parent's dotted_order with a timestamp-plus-UUID segment.

Both SDKs generate absent run IDs as UUID v7 values derived from start time; JavaScript uses an execution-order tie breaker and Python prevents an explicitly supplied child start time from preceding its parent.

Batch and multipart ingestion depend on trace_id and dotted_order: JavaScript rejects multipart creates or updates missing either field, while Python uses their presence to select its queue/compressed batch create path.
Trace sampling is keyed consistently by trace_id, with the root dotted_order segment and then run id used as fallbacks.

RunTree child creation preserves tree identity, project and client, copies parent metadata with child keys taking precedence, and adds the child to the in-memory child list; wrapper code is responsible for assembling inherited tags.

JavaScript traceable nesting propagates the current run through AsyncLocalStorage and snapshots context for async iterator and stream continuations; Python uses copied contextvars contexts and stores the active parent as a weak reference to avoid retention by captured asyncio contexts.

Distributed tracing exports full dotted_order in langsmith-trace and annotations in baggage; import reconstructs trace_id from the first segment and run id from the last segment so receiving code can create a child in the same trace.

Replica routing parsed from untrusted baggage is filtered to header-safe fields and does not accept credentials or client objects; Python additionally allow-lists replica update keys and always retains reroot.

Run persistence is a start-post followed by in-memory end and completion patch, and patch payloads intentionally omit the inputs key by default so batching cannot overwrite create inputs during create/update merging.

JavaScript traceable async iterators complete on exhaustion with aggregated chunks, record and rethrow iterator errors, and on early termination call the source iterator return method, mark the run Cancelled, preserve partial outputs, and skip waiting for unfinished children.
JavaScript ReadableStream tracing completes when the tapped reader is exhausted and explicitly records Cancelled with partial chunks before forwarding cancellation to the source reader.
For JavaScript non-stream values and promises, synchronous throws become rejected promises, completion records the error and rethrows it, and error paths avoid waiting for unfinished child runs.

Python traceable wrappers finalize and rethrow BaseException for sync, async, generator, and async-generator paths; async error cleanup is shielded from cancellation, and generator completion includes chunks accumulated before failure or close.

Python returned stream wrappers defer trace completion until exhaustion or context-manager exit and best-effort finalize on destruction; synchronous iteration records exceptions, while the asynchronous __aiter__ and __aexit__ finalization paths currently do not pass the triggering exception to trace finalization.

Attachments are binary sidecars removed from ordinary inputs; Python extracts Attachment-annotated arguments and rejects filesystem-backed or ambiguous attachment values unless dangerously_allow_filesystem is explicitly enabled.

Replica routing preserves IDs for primary destinations, deterministically remaps id, parent_run_id, trace_id, and dotted_order UUID suffixes for non-primary destinations using a project seed in both SDKs or an agent-pair seed in Python, and can reroot a destination by slicing ancestry and resetting the new root relationship.

Python groups replicas only when they share the same client and transformed payload key so serialization can be reused across authentication destinations, and supports a dedicated client per replica; JavaScript strips reroot when children inherit replica configuration so reroot applies only where explicitly configured.

Python resolves each run to project or agent addressing: a project or agent named in code suppresses the opposite environment default, a partial code-level agent pair may be completed from the environment, but environment-only project/agent conflicts and incomplete agent pairs are preserved for endpoint rejection rather than silently falling back to the default project.

Python rejects a project and agent named in the same API call, while wrapper setup resolves code-level tiers from active context and parent through invocation, decorator, and configure fallbacks, then installs the settled destination in copied context so nested traceables and directly created children inherit it.

Python distributed headers carry agent ID and environment as baggage when agent-addressed; reconstruction protects a caller-named destination from conflicting baggage, accepts only a complete baggage agent pair, and does not let an ambient agent override an upstream baggage project.
Python agent-addressed runs do not silently fall back when the feature is unavailable, and a run URL cannot be constructed before the backend-resolved project session ID is known.
Python completion updates do not newly consult agent environment variables, so a patch retains the create target or relies on run-ID lookup rather than being redirected by ambient addressing changes.

JavaScript retains an in-memory parent_run back-reference, while current Python RunTree construction uses the supplied parent only to derive parent_run_id and parent_dotted_order and does not retain that back-reference; both maintain child_runs lists for construction.
